title: The Last Abbasid: the trailer for my solo pixel-art action game set in the fall of Baghdad, 1258 (Chapter I is out, free)
author: ParfaitInitial511
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1xcngfz/video/shaiidowl1xh1/player

Baghdad, February 1258. The Mongols have breached the walls. You're Yusuf ibn Harun, one of the Caliph's last guardsmen, fighting through the burning city to save its books, its people and the friend who carried him off the wall.

* Every enemy blow glints before it lands, and its colour is the answer: white, block or parry; amber, jump; violet, parry or roll; red, roll
* Five special moves: the Storm of Blades, the Naft Flask, the Piercing Line, the Judgment of the Guard and the Second Wind
* Chapter I: four streets and a duel with Toqto Noyan, captain of a thousand
* Fully playable in English and Arabic, keyboard or gamepad

Everything in the trailer is real gameplay. I'm a solo developer from Egypt and this is my first release, so I'd love to hear what you think of the combat.

Free for Windows: [https://shehab20089.itch.io/the-last-abbasid](https://shehab20089.itch.io/the-last-abbasid)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
This is extremely impressive. 

...I cannot play it, because I am awful at these kind of games. :P 

  
 \- The walking animation needs a bit of work. The character does this weird-looking lean-back when he stops.   
 \- It is visually quite gorgeous, but I feel the larger images used for cutscene moments let it down a bit. I'd try very hard to find a way to create those same scenes but with true pixel art resolution.   
 \- In a game with a historical bent, I'd prefer hard numbers as often as possible, if you have sources for them. For this kind of experience, I prefer to hear exactly how many men the Khanate was marching with, not just that the army was large.  
 \- The parry mechanic feels a bit unforgiving to me... but, again, I can't really play these types of games no matter how much I wish I could. 

  
Good luck on this project. Your passion for the setting and the historical context really shows, and it's a unique period piece we don't see a lot of.
